[RFCS.9.4] A reader MAY use a `Checkpoint` atom as a random-access entry
point for reverse navigation: restore WM state from the following
`FactAssert` atoms, the cache from `Checkpoint.cache` ([RFCS.9.3a]), and both
clocks from `Checkpoint.clock_ns` and `Checkpoint.wall_ns` ([LTIM.2.8.5]), then
apply subsequent stream events forward. When `Checkpoint.has_wall` is false
the wall clock had no value at the checkpoint, and the reader restores it
without one, ignoring `wall_ns`. A fact restored from a `FactAssert`
atom enters with the entry stamp the atom carries ([RFCS.9.3]), not the clock
the checkpoint restored, so `dwell` and `within` read after a seek what they
read in the recording ([LTIM.2.8.6]).

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__count_after
idris.note: The source's call count after some steps of a run.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__fresh_checkpoint_breaks
idris.note: A FRESH READ IS NOT THE HELD SAMPLE: a checkpoint whose clocks were read when it was written, (3, 9), the wall clock having moved since the held sample (3, 8); the next sample is (3, 8) again so no `ClockAdvance` is written, and the seek holds (3, 9), a value the recording never held. What a writer that reads a clock outside a sample point, against [LTIM.2.8.4], costs.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__held_after
idris.note: The recorder's last recorded sample after some steps of a run.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__held_after_just
idris.note: After one or more steps the recorder's last recorded sample is the held one, whatever it was before them.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__held_at
idris.note: THE HELD SAMPLE at the last of one or more steps: what a checkpoint written there carries, on the premise the seek theorem derives from [LTIM.2.8.4].

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__mono_only_checkpoint_breaks
idris.note: THE MONOTONIC CLOCK ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH: the held sample is (3, 8), the next sample is (3, 8) again so the step writes no `ClockAdvance`, and a reader that restored the monotonic clock alone holds (3, 0) where the recording held (3, 8). 'Both clocks from `Checkpoint.clock_ns` and `Checkpoint.wall_ns`', by the reader that takes one.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__record_splits
idris.note: THE RECORDING SPLITS at any position: the atoms of the steps before, then the atoms of the steps after, recorded from the count and the held sample the first steps left. For every source, every start and every two runs.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__restamped_dwell_differs
idris.note: WHAT RE-STAMPING A RESTORED FACT WOULD COST: a fact that entered at monotonic 3, restored at a checkpoint whose clock is 7 and re-stamped with it against the clause, reads at 10 a `dwell` of 3 where the recording read 7. Computed; 'enters with the entry stamp the atom carries, not the clock the checkpoint restored', by the reader that does otherwise.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__restamped_within_reopens
idris.note: AND A `within 5` IT HAD LEFT WOULD BE OPEN AGAIN: at 10, false from the stamp of 3, true from the re-stamp of 7. Computed; '`dwell` and `within` read after a seek what they read in the recording' is what the stamp from the atom buys.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__seek
idris.note: A SEEK: the reader's clocks are the checkpoint's, and it applies the atoms after it -- the replay of [RFCS.10.5], started at the checkpoint. Working memory and the cache, the clause's other two restorations, are not modelled.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__seek_holds_what_was_held
idris.note: A SEEK FROM A CHECKPOINT THAT CARRIES THE HELD SAMPLE holds at every later input what the recording held: for every clock source, every position after a first input and every run after it. TwoClocks.idr's `ltim_2_8_5__replay_from`, applied at the position.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__seek_mono_only
idris.note: A reader whose checkpoint carries the monotonic clock alone: its wall clock is whatever it had. The refused shape.

idris.name: rfcs_9_4__steady
idris.note: A clock source that stands still at (3, 8). A fixture.
